OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'

## Summary

I implemented owner-creation validation so that missing or blank required fields (`firstName`, `lastName`, `address`, `city`, `telephone`) are rejected with **400** and a JSON body whose `errors` array names each offending field.

The baseline already fired Bean Validation via `@Valid` on the generated `OwnersApi` interface, so it returned 400 — but the response body had no `errors` array, and whitespace-blank values in non-patterned fields (`address`, `city`) slipped through. Two gaps to close.

**Changes:**

1. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — added an explicit `missingOrBlankFields(...)` check (null or `String.isBlank()`) covering all five fields. If any are missing/blank it throws a new `InvalidOwnerFieldsException` carrying the field names. This catches whitespace-blank values that Bean Validation's `@Size(min=1)`/pattern rules miss.

2. **`InvalidOwnerFieldsException`** (new) — a `RuntimeException` holding the list of offending field names.

3. **`ExceptionControllerAdvice`** — 
   - The existing `MethodArgumentNotValidException` handler (the null/pattern Bean-Validation path) now also sets an `errors` property listing the distinct failed field names.
   - A new handler for `InvalidOwnerFieldsException` returns 400 with the `errors` array (the blank-field path).

Both rejection paths now produce a consistent top-level `errors` array of field names, matching the spec and the acceptance tests (`errorRejectsMissingCity`, `errorRejectsBlankTelephone`, `functionalityAcceptsCompleteOwner`).

I kept the existing `ProblemDetail` structure and its `schemaValidationErrors` intact, only augmenting it, so other consumers of the error response are unaffected.

No git commit was made since this isn't a git repository and you didn't ask for one.
